items.title: James Trafford to Leeds: Fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history is viewed as England's next No 1 - Sky Sports
items.summary: # James Trafford to Leeds: Fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history is viewed as England's next No 1. James Trafford is bound for Leeds from Man City in a transfer initially worth £40m despite limited Premier League experience; 23-year-old becoming the fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history but those who have worked with him feel he's worth the expense. James Trafford will become the most expensive British goalkeeper in history with his £40m switch from Manchester City to Leeds. It's a hefty sum for a goalkeeper with only 32 top-flight appearances under his belt and it comes only a year after Manchester City paid £27m to re-sign him from Burnley. Trafford expected to be City's No 1 when he returned to the club he first joined as a 12-year-old last year but ended up being second-choice after the club made moved to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint-Germain late in the transfer window.

items.title: Real Madrid transfer news: Vinicius Junior to stay at the Santiago Bernabeu beyond this summer despite Arsenal interest - Sky Sports
items.summary: # Real Madrid transfer news: Vinicius Junior to stay at the Santiago Bernabeu beyond this summer despite Arsenal interest. Vinicius Junior had been a target for Arsenal, but looks set to stay at Real Madrid beyond this summer's transfer window; Jose Mourinho is understood to value the Brazilian highly; Sky Sports News revealed on Monday that talks over his future would take place this week. Vinicius Junior will be staying at Real Madrid beyond this summer, Sky Sports News has been told. The Spanish club have no intention of selling him and are confident he will agree a new contract. On Monday, *Sky Sports News* broke the news that further talks over his future between Real and his representatives will take place this week. That is with the intention of making progress on a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu. The situation regarding Vinicius Junior has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest and further talks to come.

items.title: Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off - The Guardian
items.summary: # Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off. The France Under-21s defender, who can play left-back or wingback and also operate in the centre, has attracted widespread interest this summer but Régis Le Bris now appears close to acquiring him for about £26m. Methalie will be Le Bris’s second summer signing after the arrival of the Belgium right-back Thomas Meunier, who arrived on a free transfer after leaving Lille. Newcastle, meanwhile, remain in the market for cover at left-back and right-back, with the latter position one Eddie Howe is particularly anxious to reinforce after Kieran Trippier’s departure at the end of last season. Howe’s hopes of keeping Bruno Guimarães appear to still rest on Arsenal’s willingness or otherwise to pay a fee in the region of £80m for the 28-year-old captain, who has been on a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil and is due to return to Newcastle on Friday, before travelling to a training camp at La Manga with the rest of the first-team squad.

items.title: James Trafford to Leeds: Fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history is viewed as England's next No 1 - Sky Sports
items.summary: # James Trafford to Leeds: Fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history is viewed as England's next No 1. James Trafford is bound for Leeds from Man City in a transfer initially worth £40m despite limited Premier League experience; 23-year-old becoming the fourth-most expensive goalkeeper in history but those who have worked with him feel he's worth the expense. James Trafford will become the most expensive British goalkeeper in history with his £40m switch from Manchester City to Leeds. It's a hefty sum for a goalkeeper with only 32 top-flight appearances under his belt and it comes only a year after Manchester City paid £27m to re-sign him from Burnley. Trafford expected to be City's No 1 when he returned to the club he first joined as a 12-year-old last year but ended up being second-choice after the club made moved to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint-Germain late in the transfer window.

items.title: Real Madrid transfer news: Vinicius Junior to stay at the Santiago Bernabeu beyond this summer despite Arsenal interest - Sky Sports
items.summary: # Real Madrid transfer news: Vinicius Junior to stay at the Santiago Bernabeu beyond this summer despite Arsenal interest. Vinicius Junior had been a target for Arsenal, but looks set to stay at Real Madrid beyond this summer's transfer window; Jose Mourinho is understood to value the Brazilian highly; Sky Sports News revealed on Monday that talks over his future would take place this week. Vinicius Junior will be staying at Real Madrid beyond this summer, Sky Sports News has been told. The Spanish club have no intention of selling him and are confident he will agree a new contract. On Monday, *Sky Sports News* broke the news that further talks over his future between Real and his representatives will take place this week. That is with the intention of making progress on a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu. The situation regarding Vinicius Junior has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest and further talks to come.

items.title: Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off - The Guardian
items.summary: # Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off. The France Under-21s defender, who can play left-back or wingback and also operate in the centre, has attracted widespread interest this summer but Régis Le Bris now appears close to acquiring him for about £26m. Methalie will be Le Bris’s second summer signing after the arrival of the Belgium right-back Thomas Meunier, who arrived on a free transfer after leaving Lille. Newcastle, meanwhile, remain in the market for cover at left-back and right-back, with the latter position one Eddie Howe is particularly anxious to reinforce after Kieran Trippier’s departure at the end of last season. Howe’s hopes of keeping Bruno Guimarães appear to still rest on Arsenal’s willingness or otherwise to pay a fee in the region of £80m for the 28-year-old captain, who has been on a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil and is due to return to Newcastle on Friday, before travelling to a training camp at La Manga with the rest of the first-team squad.
